name: Bengaluru Urban
headline: Migrant-labour families and school toilet gaps; thousands of dropouts counted across Bengaluru North and South.
summary: Bengaluru Urban's reported exits are tied to migration and weak tracking of children in a large, mobile population. A Bangalore Mirror report counted about 2,000 dropouts in Bengaluru South and 1,800 in Bengaluru North in 2023-24, and a 2023 High Court report found one government school in Bengaluru North and four in Bengaluru South without toilets. A statewide survey found most dropouts happen around ages 11 to 13, at the move into high school.

reasons.factor: Migration and an untracked child population
reasons.detail: A Bangalore Mirror report says migration fuels dropout in the state, and an officer said Bengaluru North's low out-of-school count (189) may reflect weak tracking in a garment-factory area.
A 2023 High Court report found one government school in Bengaluru North and four in Bengaluru South without toilets.

Children of migrant construction workers are often refused admission without local address proof, and families that keep moving for work lose continuity in schooling; transfer certificates can substitute but are inconsistently accepted.

Migrant children from other states struggle with Kannada-medium government schooling, which pushes them out; NGO bridge programmes teach Kannada, English and maths before moving them into regular classes.
Migrant labourers on daily wages say food and shelter come before children's education, and children of migrants sometimes leave school when parents return temporarily to home states.

Activists linked COVID school closures and lost incomes to dropouts, and then to child marriage; Bengaluru urban and rural together logged 279 complaints between 2020 and August 2022, with 47 marriages solemnised.

In Bandepalya (south-east Bengaluru) police began crash courses for failed SSLC students, noting that the year-long gap before retaking exams leaves them prone to drifting away. 40 of 84 enrolled had failed over five subjects.

responses.text: Gubbachi runs year-long bridge centres that prepare out-of-school migrant children in Kannada, English and maths before entering government schools.
Samridhdhi Trust operates seven bridge schools in Bengaluru with multilingual teaching, transport and sibling childcare, serving at least 700 students a year.
Bandepalya police ran a 21-day crash course with volunteer teachers and counsellors for students who failed SSLC, ahead of supplementary exams.
The Indian Social Institute study centre in Thubrahalli offers tutoring, mentoring and fee help to migrant workers' children.
